title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: this page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' and treats the modular case. Here G = GL_2, SG = SL_2, and T_ρ, T_σ are the maximal tori centralizing the elliptic elements ρ (order 6) and σ (order 4). Concretely T_ρ ≅ Res_{Z[ζ_3]/Z} G_m and T_σ ≅ Res_{Z[i]/Z} G_m. ST_ρ and ST_σ are their norm-one (determinant-one) subtori. M_{ρ,σ} is the auxiliary group scheme built earlier from these tori and their normalizers; I can only infer its definition from the neighbouring pages. R_{ρ,σ} is the 'radical' kernel of M → PG. R° is its neutral component. SR° is the kernel of κ: R° → G_m, the character to the centre G_m of GL_2.

The page computes the Z-points (absolute base Z), step by step:
1. Every unit of an imaginary quadratic order has norm 1. Hence T_ρ(Z) = ST_ρ(Z) = μ_6(Z[ζ_3]) ≅ Z/6, and T_σ(Z) = ST_σ(Z) = μ_4(Z[i]) ≅ Z/4.
2. (81) gives SR°(Z) ≅ ST_ρ(Z) × ST_σ(Z) ≅ Z/6 × Z/4.
3. The exact sequence (74), 1 → SR° → R° → G_m, together with G_m(Z) = {±1}, gives (82): R°(Z) ≅ (Z/6 × Z/4) × {±1}. The two projections are the maps R° → T° and R° → G_m.
4. (83)-(85): μ_2 = Centre(SL_2) sits inside R°. Its composite with κ is the inclusion μ_2 ⊂ G_m. So the canonical monomorphism SR° × μ_2 → R° (84) becomes an isomorphism on Z-points (85).

The purpose is bookkeeping. It identifies the finite 'radical' groups that enter the loop equation for the modular (SL_2(Z)/GL_2(Z)) case. Note that Z/4 and Z/6 are exactly the stabilizers of the elliptic points i and ρ, whose amalgam over ±1 is SL_2(Z).
errors: (84) is only a monomorphism of group schemes. Its cokernel is G_m/μ_2 ≅ G_m, so it is an isogeny-type inclusion, not an isomorphism. The isomorphism (85) holds only on Z-points, because G_m(Z) = μ_2(Z) = {±1}. Grothendieck states it correctly ('induit un isomorphisme' on Z-points), but the distinction is worth noting.

The isomorphism T_ρ × T_σ appearing in (81) is a fibre product over G (or G_ss) on the previous page. On Z-points it is written as a plain product. This is consistent only if the fibre product is over a base whose relevant Z-points are trivial, so there is a small notational ambiguity.

ideas.what: Unit groups of Z[ζ_3] and Z[i] as Z-points of the anisotropic tori centralizing the elliptic elements of GL_2(Z); the norm-one torus has the same Z-points.
ideas.modern_name: Z-points of the Weil restriction tori Res_{O_K/Z} G_m and their norm-one subtori

ideas.what: Splitting of the radical group R°(Z) as SR°(Z) × centre μ_2(Z), via G_m(Z) = μ_2(Z).
ideas.modern_name: centre of SL_2 / extension by G_m evaluated on Z-points

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine computation of finite groups of Z-points (Z/6 × Z/4 × ±1) inside Grothendieck's group-scheme framework for the modular case of the loop equation. It is correct and elementary, with nothing new beyond the internal notation.
transcription_corrections: The phrase 'on dira aussi est que l'inclusion canonique' probably reads 'on dira aussi c'est que' / 'disons que l'inclusion canonique'.
The reference '(74)' is written over another digit ('(74)' with the 7 overwritten), but 74 is the intended reference.
The page number at the bottom of the scan is 429; the transcription lacks it.
In (84), the left vertical chain is SR° = ST_ρ×ST_σ ⊂ M°_{ρ,σ}(0), and μ_2 is identified with Centre(SG), which is underlined in the image.
